1.explanation: All of the code that decides how to render table rows and cells—including the snippet column—lives in table.js and its Handlebars partials under formatters/partials/. table.js is where the Markdown library is invoked (unconditionally) on each cell value, and the partials define the HTML and text templates that wrap those values. Since the bug is that snippets beginning with backticks are still run through Markdown, these are the files to update: in table.js add a check to bypass Markdown processing when a cell’s string starts with a backtick, and adjust the corresponding partial templates so they emit the raw snippet instead of a Markdown-rendered SafeString.
1.bug_scenario: When a code snippet value begins with a backtick (‘`’), the table formatter still feeds it through the Markdown-to-HTML (and Markdown-to-text) pass. Any underscores (`_`) become … tags and any bracketed link syntax (`[text](url)`) becomes …, mangling the snippet. In both the HTML report and the plain-text (“pretty”) output the snippet is supposed to remain verbatim if it starts with a backtick, but currently it does not.

2.explanation: All of the code that wraps snippets in Markdown fences and then invokes the Markdown-to‐HTML (or Markdown-to‐text) conversion lives in the TableFormatter and its templates. • table.js constructs the fenced‐code blocks and calls out to the Markdown parser unconditionally. • table.html and table.txt are the Handlebars templates used for HTML and pretty text output, respectively, and they render whatever the helper in table.js returns. To fix the bug we need to change table.js so that if the snippet string begins with a backtick, it bypasses the Markdown processor (and likely adjust the templates to render it raw).
2.bug_scenario: When the TableFormatter renders a snippet that begins with a backtick (`` ` ``), it still runs the entire string through its Markdown pass—so any underscores (`_`) become `<em>` tags and any bracketed link syntax (`[text](url)`) becomes `<a>` tags. In the provided screenshots you can see parts of the JavaScript collapsed into `<em>` elements around zeroes and `<a>` tags around link text, even though the snippet should have remained verbatim once it starts with a backtick.
